newsitem.title: USA: CFTC seeks comments on CME boneless beef contracts.
newsitem.headline: CFTC seeks comments on CME boneless beef contracts.

text.p: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said Tuesday it had invited comments on CME proposals for 90-percent lean boneless beef and 50-percent lean beef trimmings futures contracts.
Comments must be received by October 23, the CFTC said.

The Chicago Mercantile Exchange is already designated as a contract market in beef trimmings, but the contract is dormant. CME sought to amend the contract months and other specifications of the dormant contract.

For the 90-percent lean contract, the cash settlement price would be based on USDA-reported daily weighted average price and volume of sales for 90-percent lean boneless beef FOB Omaha and East Texas-Oklahoma.

For the beef trimmings contract, the cash settlement price would be based on daily weighted average price and volume of sales reported by USDA for 50-percent lean boneless beef FOB Omaha in the National Carlot Meat Report.
The trading unit for both contracts would be 20,000 pounds.
The maximum daily price fluctuation for both contracts would be $0.030 per pound, which could be raised to $.045 per pound under certain conditions.
The CME has said the contracts respond to increased interest among cash market participants for ways to manage price risk.
Ground beef, which is made from grinding boneless beef, has increased to more than 50 percent of all beef consumed in the United States from 25 percent in 1975.
